change.title: pr-36882-flat
change.description: Add rolling-updates feature flag and compatibility framework
change.author: Cristian Sotomayor

findings.title: Doc says the Operator fails without `rolling-updates`, but no Operator code checks the feature
findings.body: The new CAUTION says: "Otherwise, the {project_name} Operator will fail." In this checkout the Operator never reads the feature. `UpgradeLogicFactory.create` (operator/src/main/java/org/keycloak/operator/upgrade/UpgradeLogicFactory.java:35-43) picks `AlwaysRecreateUpgradeLogic` or `RecreateOnImageChangeUpgradeLogic` from `UpdateSpec.findUpdateStrategy` alone. A grep of operator/src/main finds no use of `Profile`, `rolling-updates` or `update-compatibility`. `UpgradeTest` also only enables the feature when a strategy is set; the `null` case returns early (UpgradeTest.java:105-107). So `strategy: Recreate` without the feature still works, and the sentence is not backed by the code. Either describe the real behaviour, for example that the strategy is only supported as a preview with the feature enabled, or add the Operator-side check. If a later change in this PR adds that check, ignore this.

findings.title: RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE changes from 4 to 3
findings.body: The exit code for "recreate upgrade required" moves from 4 to 3, so that 4 can mean the feature is disabled. This was 4 before the change, and any script that tested `== 4` now sees "recreate" as 3. The guide's table (docs/guides/server/update-compatibility.adoc:128-134) now lists 3 for recreate and 4 for the disabled feature, so docs and code agree. Because the command is preview, this is probably acceptable. It is still an observable change to a scriptable interface, and neither the PR description nor the guide mentions it. Consider saying so in the PR description or the upgrade notes.

contracts.action: update-compatibility `check` and `metadata` subcommands now exit early when the `rolling-updates` feature is disabled
contracts.equivalent_path: Normal path in the same `run()`: print the preview warning, call `validateConfig()`, then compute the result and call `picocli.exit(result.exitCode())`. `UpdateCompatibilityMetadata.run()` has the same shape.
contracts.before_after: Before: the commands always ran. After: the gate runs first, so it prints an error via `printFeatureDisabled()`, calls `picocli.exit(4)` and returns. It skips the preview warning and config validation, so a missing `--file` is not reported in that case. `Picocli.exit` hard-exits only when the code is non-zero and the launch is not a test launch (Picocli.java:203-207). In test launch mode it just returns, and the added `return` stops the command from continuing.
contracts.visible_effect: The user sees the "Unable to use this command..." message on stderr and exit code 4. With `--features=rolling-updates` behaviour is unchanged. UpdateCommandDistTest covers both the disabled message and the enabled paths.
contracts.failure_mode: `Profile.isFeatureEnabled` dereferences `getInstance()`, which is null until the profile is configured. Profile configuration happens through `Environment.getCurrentOrCreateFeatureProfile`, called from PropertyMappers. I did not trace that this always runs before `run()` for these commands, but the existing dist test is written to exercise it.

contracts.action: Operator CR and test image enable `rolling-updates` (UpgradeTest feature spec, Dockerfile `--features`)
contracts.before_after: Before: the test only set `UnsupportedSpec` and `updateSpec`. After: `updateSpec` is set first, then the feature spec, with `setEnabledFeatures(List.of(ROLLING_UPDATES.getKey()))`. For the `null` strategy parameter the method returns early, so the feature is not enabled in that case.
contracts.visible_effect: CR gets `features.enabled: [rolling-updates]` for the RECREATE case only. The Operator does not read the feature today, so the test outcome does not depend on it.
contracts.failure_mode: None found. `FeatureSpec` serialises to `enabled` / `disabled`, which matches the doc YAML.

summary: I found no defects that block this part. I raised two low-severity items. The first is a doc claim in advanced-configuration.adoc that the Operator will fail without `rolling-updates`, which no Operator code in this checkout implements. The second is that the recreate exit code changes from 4 to 3 without any mention in the PR description or upgrade notes. The CLI gate in `check` and `metadata`, the new exit code 4, the Dockerfile `--features` flag, the UpgradeTest change and the guide table all look consistent with each other. I did not read the code that confirms the profile is always configured before `run()`. The existing dist test is written to exercise that path.
